source.title: New behaviorally-based cross-sectional reversal portfolios in the cryptocurrency market and market uncertainty

research_question: Does proximity to the formation-period low identify crypto assets with stronger subsequent weekly reversal after realistic costs?
hypothesis: Among liquid Binance perpetuals, assets still trading close to their recent formation-period low subsequently outperform assets that sit far above that low, consistent with lowest-price anchoring and delayed reversal.
economic_mechanism: Investors anchor on salient lows after drawdowns; assets that remain near the anchor may be temporarily underpriced, while assets already far above the anchor have already realized the rebound.
source_deviation: The accessible paper abstract states that the lowest formation-period price is the anchor but does not expose the exact decomposition formula. This test therefore preregisters a simple transparent proxy: negative distance of prior close from the rolling low. It is not claimed as an exact replication.
universe_rule: Each Monday require exact causal history and valid next-week execution data; retain the top 50 contemporaneously eligible contracts by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume.

feature.direction: Long highest signal (closest to recent low), short lowest signal (farthest above recent low).

portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral top/bottom quintiles, 0.5 gross per side.
rebalance: Weekly Monday 00:00 UTC; signal and liquidity end Sunday; execute at Monday open and hold to next Monday open.

costs.funding: not modeled; any positive result remains exploratory

development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive top-minus-bottom weekly spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 lookbacks positive.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; positive at 2x costs; >=2/3 lookbacks positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; exclude BTC/ETH positive; remove strongest contributor positive; one-day delayed holding remains positive; DSR reported.
